axes.brief:
One-party national leadership, controlled candidature and subordinate courts constrain competitive accountability. Focused review prioritises implemented competitive renewal and effective oversight; formal powers in controlled institutions are not automatically democratic accountability.
Focused six-question reassessment: Technical institutions are politically directed and public legislative proposals remain within controlled representative procedures. Citizen proposals and state-called popular consultations are not automatically the independent binding ordinary-law initiative in question.
axes.counterEvidence:
Formal suffrage, National Assembly powers and recall exist. Union participation in candidate commissions is not union-only appointment of the government; legal checks and actual independence differ. The bank also credits rejection of specific unelected alternatives (experts, unions, military) and narrower formal rights. These literal answers are retained where supported; the resulting percentage is not a probability or validated democracy index. Restrictions on women inform political participation where relevant, without automatically transferring Authority vs Liberty scores.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Technical institutions are politically directed and public legislative proposals remain within controlled representative procedures. Citizen proposals and state-called popular consultations are not automatically the independent binding ordinary-law initiative in question.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: National leadership operates through one-party controlled elections and assembly selection, not regular competitive leadership contests.

Educated assumption: Neutral is the most likely response to the revised claim “Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: One-party national leadership, controlled candidature and subordinate courts constrain competitive accountability. Focused review prioritises implemented competitive renewal and effective oversight; formal powers in controlled institutions are not automatically democratic accountability. Focused interpretation: Technical institutions are politically directed and public legislative proposals remain within controlled representative procedures. Citizen proposals and state-called popular consultations are not automatically the independent binding ordinary-law initiative in question. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  This is a substantive conditional judgement: the described case for functioning government or collective continuity competes with the described limits on independent discretion or public consent. Neither unqualified permission nor unqualified prohibition best represents that tension. It is not a default for absent evidence. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.
Educated assumption: Voting from sixteen is not contingent on intelligence or education; legal capacity, residency and disqualification exceptions qualify universality.

The retained sourced research records: One-party national leadership, controlled candidature and subordinate courts constrain competitive accountability. Citizen proposals and state-called popular consultations are not automatically the independent binding ordinary-law initiative in question. This permits temporary lawmaking before a vote but expressly retains parliamentary rejection and expiry. It is not the previous permission to override an actual parliamentary rejection; primary legislation and delegated emergency instruments can differ.
